transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (ACME Head of ML), Sofia Alvarez (Infra Lead), Ben Cho (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): brief notes, may be imperfect.

Topics: Dedicated capacity, reserved GPUs, burst strategy, autoscaling, isolation/VPC, encryption/KMS, SOC2, SSO, pricing/commitment

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh. this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with Priya our solutions engineer. how are you doing today?
[00:05] Carlos Mendez: good, thanks. yep, we, we wanted to dive into Dedicated — we've been evaluating hosted vs dedicated; main concerns are data isolation and predictable throughput for our production NLU endpoints.
[00:12] Priya Raman: great, yeah, we'll go through typical reserved capacity patterns, burst options, and a little bit of the autoscale logic. quick qual question, what's your target p95 latency and roughly how many concurrent requests at peak?
[00:20] Carlos Mendez: target p95 is around 450ms for the 2k token flows, we have about 300-400 concurrent realtime requests at peak but batch/async loads come in overnight.
[00:28] Sofia Alvarez: add to that, our security team requires tenant isolation and we prefer VPC/private deployment if possible; at minimum, logs and payloads can't be stored on third-party multi-tenant buckets.
[00:36] Ben Cho: yep SOC 2 type 2 already in our checklist. also need to know how KMS/HSM integrates if we bring our own keys.
[00:42] Jordan Lee: understood. quick context: Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools – you can pin capacity to a tenant with a commitment. the control plane remains optioned by you in Private or managed in Dedicated for enterprise customers; for Hosted we do multi-tenant. we often see customers pick Dedicated when their isolation + throughput predictability needs are high.
[00:55] Priya Raman: on the runtime side, a couple of things to call out — we recommend sizing based on concurrent token throughput rather than just qps. for 2k token requests at 400 conc, that maps to a certain token-per-second estimate. we typically map that to number of A100/80GB or equivalent GPUs and factor in batching.
[01:10] Carlos Mendez: can you clarify batching impact? we try to keep latency tight, so big batch windows are not ideal.
[01:15] Priya Raman: absolutely. Redwood's runtime does continuous batching with small batching windows, and you can set latency SLOs that prevent excessive batching. for Dedicated you get predictable batching behavior since the capacity is reserved — less noisy neighbors. still, if you want ultra-low latency you might trade off some efficiency (and cost).
[01:30] Sofia Alvarez: how does burst work? we have spiky campaigns and would like a burst to a shared pool rather than overprovisioning reserved capacity.
[01:35] Jordan Lee: good question. we offer a burst policy: if reserved pool is saturated, requests can overflow to a soft-shared pool (hosted capacity) subject to compatibility rules (model variant, quantization). there's a fallback cost premium; it's intended for short spikes.
[01:48] Priya Raman: to add, you can configure max burst percentage and fallback latency SLOs — so you won't silently exceed budget. some customers prefer a hard cap that rejects when reserved capacity is full.
[01:58] Ben Cho: from security standpoint, if we burst into hosted pool, is PII or model inputs leaving our VPC? what guarantees?
[02:05] Jordan Lee: when bursting, payloads are still routed and logged per your tenancy policies; however, if you're on Dedicated with strict isolation the default is to not allow burst into shared host unless you explicitly opt-in. for Private deployments we can guarantee no cross-tenant hosting. we'll also provide flow diagrams for logs and encryption.
[02:22] Carlos Mendez: are there autoscale policies? like scale up GPU count vs add more pods? what's the reaction time?
[02:28] Priya Raman: Dedicated supports two main autoscale levers: horizontal (add more worker instances / pods with GPUs) and vertical (add more reserved GPUs in the pool via warm standby). warm standby takes minutes depending on infra, whereas horizontal scaling in-cluster is faster but bounded by your reserved pool. for cross-region failover it's also supported with routing policies.
[02:45] Carlos Mendez: minutes for warm standby could be rough for our use case. we have campaign spikes that last 10s of minutes.
[02:50] Priya Raman: in that case we usually recommend a baseline reserved pool sized for steady-state plus a burst budget configured to the hosted pool, or use a small buffer of hot spare GPUs you keep reserved to absorb short spikes. that way you avoid cold spin-up.
[03:06] Sofia Alvarez: what's the minimum commit for reserved capacity? and do you do monthly vs annual billing?
[03:12] Jordan Lee: typical commitments are monthly or annual; pricing improves with longer commits. minimums vary by region/hardware — I'll include specifics in the pricing deck. for example indicative starting block is 2 x A100-equivalents as a minimum in some regions.
[03:24] Carlos Mendez: also curious about GPU types — we run models derived from Llama 2 variants and some internal fine-tunes. quantized models might be fine. do you have recommendations?
[03:34] Priya Raman: yes, we have model profiles. for Llama2-13B-like models, Q4/8 quantized on A100/80GB or H100-like gives a good latency/cost balance. we'll attach our model catalog and profiling notes.
[03:45] Ben Cho: audit logs and RBAC — do you provide immutable audit logs and SSO integrations?
[03:50] Jordan Lee: yes, Dedicated includes audit logs, RBAC, and SAML/SSO integrations. for Private deployments we can integrate with your enterprise KMS/HSM and provide more stringent key custody. we'll share the security pack.
[03:59] Carlos Mendez: any nuance on data residency? some of our customers are EU-only.
[04:03] Jordan Lee: you can pin the dedicated cluster to region(s) for residency. Private deployments can be on-prem or VPC peered in region. we support region pinning and cross-region replication options for redundancy.
[04:15] Carlos Mendez: great. can we talk about cost math — what does reserved vs burst cost look like?
[04:20] Jordan Lee: reserved is priced as committed GPU-hours plus a software platform fee; burst to hosted has a usage premium per token. grossly simplified, reserved is cheaper per-token but you pay for idle when underutilized. we'll include some worked examples in the deck matched to your traffic traces.
[04:33] Priya Raman: one practical tip: enable prefix/KV cache for chat-like workloads; it reduces token throughput significantly and can reduce effective GPU needs. we have tooling to estimate cache hit rates given your conversation length distribution.
[04:45] Sofia Alvarez: what's the rollback behavior for model rollouts? if a new model regresses, can we automatically fallback?
[04:49] Priya Raman: yes, Redwood supports rollouts and automatic fallback policies — you can set canary percentages and automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts tied to your evals.
[04:58] Carlos Mendez: do you support private control plane? we'd prefer control plane in our VPC for compliance.
[05:03] Jordan Lee: yes that's the Redwood Private option. for Dedicated we offer a managed control plane with strict tenant isolation; Private gives you full control plane in your VPC or on-prem. We'll clarify networking tradeoffs in the doc.
[05:13] Ben Cho: on KMS — can we bring our own keys and have the platform not see plaintext?
[05:18] Priya Raman: yes, BYOK via supported KMS/HSM providers; keys are used for encrypting at rest and in some flows for in-flight tokenization — we can provide details in the security pack.
[05:27] Carlos Mendez: what's the typical onboarding time for Dedicated? from PO to prod?
[05:31] Jordan Lee: for Dedicated it's usually 4-8 weeks depending on integrations (SSO, KMS, VPC peering). Private on-prem can be longer. we'll put a proposed onboarding timeline in the proposal.
[05:42] Sofia Alvarez: can you run a quick scenario: we have 400 conc, 2k tokens, 95% within 450ms — how many A100 equivalents?
[05:50] Priya Raman: rough rule: A single A100-80GB serving a quantized 13B model with small batching might do ~50-80 conc at 2k tokens with our latency SLOs; so you'd be looking at 6-8 GPUs plus buffer. exact number depends on batching and cache. we'll run a detailed perf estimate with your traffic trace.
[06:06] Carlos Mendez: okay, that helps. what about high availability across AZs? if AZ goes down do we failover automatically?
[06:12] Jordan Lee: yes, we support multi-AZ deployments; Dedicated can be deployed across AZs with cross-AZ replication and routing. there is some added cost for cross-AZ warm spares.
[06:21] Carlos Mendez: fantastic. any gotchas, like noisy neighbor in Dedicated?
[06:25] Priya Raman: with Dedicated reserved pools you largely avoid noisy neighbor issues since the pool is single-tenant. the main gotcha is underprovisioning for spikes — that's why we discuss burst and hot-spares.
[06:34] Ben Cho: can you send compliance artifacts? we need SOC 2 + pen test reports before legal signs off.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll share SOC 2 and our security pack; for pen tests we can provide summaries and coordinate NDAs if required.
[06:45] Carlos Mendez: timeline — we want to have a pilot by end of Q1 2026. is that realistic?
[06:50] Jordan Lee: yes, pilot by end of Q1 is feasible. we'll scope a pilot: 2-4 week pilot using Dedicated reserved small pool + performance targets.
[06:58] Priya Raman: next steps recap: Jordan will send pricing deck and commitment options; Priya will share GPU sizing spreadsheet and profiling docs; ACME to share 1-week traffic traces and security contacts.
[07:08] Jordan Lee: perfect, thanks everyone. any final questions?
[07:10] Sofia Alvarez: no, thanks. we'll wait for the deck.
[07:12] Carlos Mendez: thanks all.

End of transcript.
